chapter_theme: The Siva lingam (சிவலிங்கம்): the Lord pervades sea, wind and fire too widely to be walked round, yet there is a way to circle him, by water, flowers and his name; the nine forms together are the lingam, and restraining the breath through the inner flame leads to the supreme state.
structure_note: A question and its answer (1773, 1774), a verse of worship (1775), the lingam as the nine forms (1776) and a yogic verse (1777). The alternative title சிவகுரு is not developed in the verses.

1773.reading: The roaring sea, the water of the earth, the spreading wind and the fire that dwells in things: he stretches long and wide in their ordered array, and I do not know how to bound him and walk round him.
1773.nuance: வலம்செய்தல் is circumambulation, walking round a shrine in worship. The difficulty is that the Lord is the elements themselves, so there is no outside from which to circle him.

1774.reading: There is one way here to bound him and walk round him: for those who bear the flowing Ganga water and flowers and can utter his name and know him, the one with twisted matted hair does not go off anywhere and hide.
1774.nuance: The answer to 1773 is worship with water, flowers and the name, joined to knowing (உணரவல்லார்). புரைத்து எங்கும் போகான் may also mean that he does not slip away through any gap.

1775.reading: We have seen the Lord as one alone; as I worship his pair of feet as the good, the First Lord gives grace then and there, so that the five senses are conquered and lie subdued and one rejoices.
1775.nuance: அன்று என்று is unclear: 'on that day', or 'saying it is not so'. மிகக்கிடந்து may describe the senses lying overcome or the devotee lying prostrate.

1776.reading: Brahma who blossomed, Vishnu, Rudra, Mahesa, the five-faced one who gives fruit, supreme bindu and nada, Shakti who gives good and Siva: taking these forms, the lingam that gives fruit is the supreme Nandi.
1776.nuance: These are the nine forms of 1764, named. ஐம்முகன் (the five-faced) is Sadasiva. Calling the lingam பராநந்தி makes the guru's name, Nandi, the name of the whole.

1777.reading: Going through the red flame that rises, while the breath rises only as far as the body allows, if one contemplates what is to be joined and what goes on leaving it, and restrains it, that is the supreme state.
1777.nuance: செஞ்சுடர் (red flame) is taken as the inner fire or kundalini, and ஆவி as the breath. The second and third lines are hard to construe: they may contrast the breath that is held with the breath that goes out.

links.note: 1773 says the Lord is too vast to be walked round; 1774 answers that water, flowers and his name, with knowing, are the way to circle him.

A near-repeat: 1773 and 2836 both list sea, water, wind and fire and end நீண்டகன்றானை வரைத்து (வரைந்து) வலம்செயு மாறுஅறி யேனே, I do not know how to bound him and walk round him. 2836 adds ஆகாசம் and நிலத்திடை வானிடை; the claim is the same, that a Lord who is the elements has no outside to circle.

1774 gives the one way to 'circle' the boundless Lord: bearing water and flowers and uttering his name (உரைத்து அவன் நாமம்). 1831 says worship, the gods and the sea are all his, and பேராயிரமும் பிரான்திரு நாமமும் are a way that never sates. Both put the name at the centre of worship of a Lord who cannot be bounded.

Kural 6 promises long life to those who keep the path of the one who quenched the five senses (பொறிவாயில் ஐந்தவித்தான்). In 1775 the devotee worships the feet and the First Lord gives grace so that வென்றுஐம் புலமும் மிகக்கிடந்து, the five senses lie conquered. The Kural credits the Lord with the quenching and asks the devotee to follow; Tirumular has the Lord's grace do the quenching in the devotee.

Both name the same nine: அயன், மால், உருத்திரன், மகேசன், ஐம்முகன், விந்து, நாதம், சத்தி, சிவன். 1731 says Sadasiva is what is common to them all (சாதாரணமாம் சதாசிவம்); 1776 says the lingam that takes these forms is பராநந்தி. Both make the nine one, naming the one differently.

1807 lists the nine forms from சிவமொடு சத்தி down to the lotus-born (பதுமத்தோன்) and says he dances as these nine (நவம்அவை யாகி நடிப்பவன்). 1776 lists the same nine from Brahma up and calls their lingam பராநந்தி. The order is reversed but the claim, one Lord in nine forms, is the same.

Both describe going through the red flame: 1777 செஞ்சுடர் ஊடுசென்று, 2719 செஞ்சுடர் மண்டலத்து ஊடுசென்று அப்புறம். 1777 ends in பரகதி through restraint of breath; 2719 ends in a state where the Lord never leaves the heart, reached through the five letters. The shared phrase marks one inner passage reached by breath in one verse and by mantra in the other.

source_issues: 1777: lines 2 and 3 are hard to construe and may be corrupt.
